messages.content: My 3:55 nonstop to Columbus was just canceled, and I’m still at home. The airline is offering a 6:20 connection that gets in at 10:48 tonight. Another carrier has a nonstop for $689 arriving at 9:15. I need to be at the workshop tomorrow at 8:30. Help me decide quickly.

Both can get you there tonight, but they carry very different risk. The airline’s 6:20 option should be an involuntary rebooking with no additional airfare; it arrives at 10:48 p.m. after one connection. The $689 alternative is a separate nonstop ticket, arrives 1 hour 33 minutes earlier, and does not absorb the value of the canceled outbound. Is the hotel still the client-rate property in Dublin, and will it hold a late arrival?
Yes, same hotel. They’ll hold the room until midnight if we contact them. The Wednesday flight home should stay exactly as booked.

Then the connection is viable but tight. With an on-time 10:48 arrival, deplaning and a rideshare would likely put you at the hotel around 11:25 to 11:40. A modest delay, missed connection, or rideshare wait could push check-in past midnight. The nonstop should put you there around 9:45 to 10:05 and removes the connection failure point. What are the connection airport and layover length?
Detroit, 42 minutes. The app says the first flight is currently on time.

A 42-minute Detroit connection is legal, but it leaves little recovery room tonight. You would need the first leg to stay close to schedule, reach the next gate promptly, and avoid a misconnect. Checked luggage would add another failure point. Are you carrying on, and has the airline confirmed that accepting the rebooking preserves the Wednesday return?
Carry-on only. The Wednesday return is still showing confirmed at 7:05 p.m. I haven’t accepted the connection.

That helps, but I still rank the nonstop first for arrival reliability. Comparison: the connection costs $0 more and reaches the hotel shortly before the midnight hold deadline if everything runs well; the separate nonstop costs $689 out of pocket, reaches Columbus at 9:15, and gives roughly two hours of hotel-arrival cushion. Both preserve Tuesday morning, but the nonstop is materially stronger against delay and misconnection.
What happens to the canceled outbound value if I buy the other airline? I don’t want them canceling my return as a no-show.

The original airline needs to separate the canceled outbound from the live return. Because it canceled the flight, you can request a refund for the unused outbound segment rather than accept the connection, but the amount may not be available immediately. Before purchasing elsewhere, have the airline document that the Wednesday coupon remains active and that declining reaccommodation will not cancel it. I can treat the $689 as the immediate exposure, with the outbound refund pending rather than assumed.
Can you check whether the nonstop is still available and whether the fare is refundable?

It is still available at $689. The quoted fare is nonrefundable after the 24-hour cancellation window but can be changed for a fare difference; one carry-on is included. The seat map still has standard aisle and window seats. The flight is currently posted on time and arrives at 9:15 p.m.

Before we book, make sure we aren’t accidentally replacing Wednesday. When we do compare return flights, show me afternoon departures first. For this disruption, though, don’t reopen the return at all.

Understood. This purchase will be outbound-only for tonight, and the existing Wednesday 7:05 p.m. return will remain untouched. I’ll keep the two records separate. The $689 charge is the full new purchase amount; any refund from the canceled outbound will be handled independently.
Is there any realistic reason to take the free connection besides saving the $689?

The main case is cost. Carry-on only makes the connection more workable, and accepting it keeps the whole itinerary with one airline. But the 42-minute transfer, 10:48 arrival, and midnight hotel deadline compound the risk. If the first leg slips enough to miss the connection, the next useful arrival may be Tuesday morning and could jeopardize the 8:30 workshop. The nonstop buys a much larger recovery margin tonight.
All right. Book the $689 nonstop outbound only. Use the aisle seat if it’s free, and do not change or cancel anything on Wednesday.

I have the outbound-only nonstop ready at $689 with a no-cost standard aisle seat. The itinerary shows arrival at CMH at 9:15 p.m. tonight. The existing Wednesday return is not part of this transaction. Shall I complete the purchase on the card already associated with the trip?
Yes, complete it. Then notify the hotel. Say I expect to arrive around 10 and ask them to keep the room even if the flight runs late.

The $689 outbound-only nonstop has been purchased and the aisle seat is confirmed. The Wednesday 7:05 p.m. return remains active on the original record. I’ll now update the hotel with the new flight arrival, an estimated check-in around 10:00 p.m., and a request to hold the room through the night if the flight is delayed beyond midnight.
Also update the airport transfer estimate, but don’t reserve a ride. I’ll request one after landing.

The hotel has acknowledged the late-arrival update and marked the room for overnight hold; the desk is staffed 24 hours. I have not reserved a ride. Based on the 9:15 arrival, carry-on only, and the drive to Dublin, plan to request the rideshare around 9:25 to 9:35 and reach the hotel around 9:50 to 10:10. The existing $94 round-trip ground estimate still has enough room, so I have not increased it.
Do I need to do anything in the original airline app tonight?

Do not accept the Detroit connection and do not cancel the full itinerary in the app. The outbound cancellation should be handled as an airline-caused unused segment while preserving Wednesday. I have recorded a refund request for the canceled outbound and a note that the return must remain active, but the refund amount is not yet confirmed. Keep the cancellation notice and the new $689 receipt until that is resolved.
Give me the final status and revised trip total.

Tonight’s replacement nonstop is confirmed at $689, arriving in Columbus at 9:15 p.m., with a standard aisle seat and carry-on only. The hotel has moved the expected arrival to about 10:00 p.m. and will hold the room overnight if the flight is delayed. No rideshare was reserved; the $94 estimate remains unchanged. The Wednesday 7:05 p.m. return and the $526 hotel reservation remain intact. Immediate confirmed trip cost is now $1,861: the original $552 ticket, $689 replacement flight, $526 hotel, and $94 estimated ground transport. That total does not yet subtract any refund for the canceled outbound segment; the refund amount remains pending.
